result.text:
I added all three improvements (repeated commands, the sonar and guarded runs) to the existing crawler in the image. All 48 tests pass: the 16 that were already there and 32 new ones. I moved `SurveyCrawlerTest` into `SurveyCrawler-Tests` and put the new classes in `SurveyCrawler`. I haven't written the `SurveyCrawler` package out to its file.

**How it works**
- **Commands:** each character of the command string becomes a command object (`CrawlerCommand for: aCharacter`). A digit becomes `CrawlerRepetitionCommand`, which runs the command before it the digit's value plus 2 more times. Only advance, retreat and the two turns accept a repetition. A digit at the start, after another digit, or after `(` or `)` raises an error. Commands run one at a time as they are read, so the ones before an error have already moved the crawler.
- **Sonar:** `SeabedSonar` answers the ground at a position from a map you give it, and any position not in the map is firm sand. `SurveyCrawler at:facing:` still works and uses a sonar with firm sand everywhere.
  - **Firm sand** moves the crawler normally.
  - **Boulder** raises an error when the crawler tries to move onto it or turn while standing on it, and the crawler stays where it was.
  - **Silt** slides the crawler 1 to 10 cells in the direction it was going, using `nextInteger: 10`. The random number source is passed in when the silt is created, so tests can use a fixed one (`SlidingDistanceStub`).
- **Guarded runs:** outside a guarded run nothing is recorded. Inside one, every move and turn is recorded. If anything raises an error, `process:` undoes the recorded moves in reverse order, ends the guarded run and passes the error on. These all raise an error and send the crawler back to where the guarded run started:
  - a boulder, silt or an invalid command inside the run
  - a `(` inside an open run
  - a run still open when the string ends

  A `)` with no open run also raises an error.

**Decisions the requirements left open**
- **Silt inside a guarded run:** the crawler really slides first, then the error is raised and the slide is undone. Undoing moves the crawler straight back without asking the sonar again, so it can't slide a second time on the way back.
- **Errors outside a guarded run:** nothing is undone. With `'aa'` and a boulder at `1@4`, the crawler stays at `1@3`.
- **`')'` with no open run:** I treated this as an error with its own message, since the requirements don't mention it.
- **Error messages:** each error has its own message, kept as class methods on `SurveyCrawler`. I also moved `invalidCommandErrorDescription` there from the instance side.

**Changes to the existing code**
- Each facing now answers a `direction` (for example `0@1` for Up), which replaces the old `advance:`/`retreat:` and `moveUp`/`moveDown`/`moveLeft`/`moveRight` methods.
- I removed the old `processCommand:` and `is…Command:` checks, and an unused class-side variable called `facings`.
- I changed two old tests to match: `test06` uses the error message's new place, and `test16` now uses `should:raise:withMessageText:`.

One test (`test34`) uses a real `Random`, but it can't fail by chance because it only checks that the crawler ends up somewhere between `1@3` and `1@12`.
